claim_verdicts.evidence: "For headless Services, a cluster IP is not allocated, kube-proxy does not handle these Services, and there is no load balancing or proxying done by the platform for them." (refs mirror is the v1.37 site; the Headless Services text is unchanged long-standing behaviour.)

service.md: "For headless Services that define selectors, the endpoints controller creates EndpointSlices ... and modifies the DNS configuration to return A or AAAA records ... that point directly to the Pods backing the Service." dns-pod-service.md: "the Pod needs to be ready in order to have a record unless publishNotReadyAddresses=True is set on the Service." True as the default; round 2: section 4 no longer says "ready" of rabbitmq-headless.

statefulset.md: "The domain managed by this Service takes the form: $(service name).$(namespace).svc.cluster.local, where \"cluster.local\" is the cluster domain. As each Pod is created, it gets a matching DNS subdomain, taking the form: $(podname).$(governing service domain), where the governing service is defined by the serviceName field"; note: "Cluster Domain will be set to cluster.local unless otherwise configured." Output resolves rabbitmq-0.rabbitmq-headless.donhang.svc.cluster.local.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/kubernetes-website statefulset.md L196-202, L229-231; examples/don-hang outputs/stage-3/scripts/k8s/headless-dns.txt L9

claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: ledger and section 4 now read "no Pod a name built from the Pod's own name". dns-pod-service.md: per-Pod FQDN records come from hostname+subdomain with a matching headless Service; CoreDNS also serves IP-derived <pod-ipv4-address>.<service-name>... records, which the new wording no longer denies. statefulset.md ties $(podname).$(governing service domain) to serviceName.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/kubernetes-website dns-pod-service.md L118-130, L150-152, L211-216; statefulset.md L196-202

claim_verdicts.evidence: Round 2: ledger and sections 4/6 now say nothing keeps the old IP and that it changed in the run, not that a new IP is guaranteed. headless-dns.txt: "rabbitmq-0's address changed: yes", "... -> the new address: yes". statefulset.md: Pod DNS subdomain is $(podname).$(governing service domain), so the name follows the Pod name.

dns-pod-service.md: "\"Normal\" (not headless) Services are assigned DNS A and/or AAAA records ... with a name of the form my-svc.my-namespace.svc.cluster-domain.example. This resolves to the cluster IP of the Service." service.md: a headless Service is a ClusterIP Service with .spec.clusterIP set to None, "not the same as leaving the .spec.clusterIP field unset". Output: rabbitmq -> the Service's address: yes.
claim_verdicts.source: refs/kubernetes-website dns-pod-service.md L74-77; service.md L897-900; headless-dns.txt L7

Clustering page: "If the hostname changes, a new empty database is created." Run: ls /var/lib/rabbitmq/mnesia prints rabbit@rabbitmq-0.rabbitmq-headless.donhang.svc.cluster.local.

rabbitmq.com Configuration (WebFetch summary): RABBITMQ_NODENAME default on Unix "rabbit@$HOSTNAME"; RABBITMQ_USE_LONGNAME: "When set to true this will cause RabbitMQ to use fully qualified names to identify nodes." Run: rabbitmqctl eval 'node().' prints 'rabbit@rabbitmq-0.rabbitmq-headless.donhang.svc.cluster.local'.
